intro-0.text: Zcash's shielded pools are a vault. Sender, receiver and amount stay hidden.

intro-1.text: But the vault has doors. And the doors are public.

leak-0.text: Every time money enters or leaves, the exact amount lands on the public chain.

leak-1.text: Someone shielded 2.50121076 ZEC. Nine minutes later, 2.50106076 came out: the same amount, minus the 15,000 zatoshi fee.

stat-0.text: Leakscope models an observer with only the public chain. Over 75 days since the Ironwood pool launched, 24.6% of withdrawals can be linked: 6.2% by exact amount, the rest by round trips.

acc-0.text: Are the links real? We run the same rule backwards in time. Money can't leave before it arrives, so every backward match is a coincidence.

acc-1.text: That measures the false-link rate on the real chain: the fastest links are about 99% precise.

check-0.text: Check takes a transaction in the indexed range and shows what anyone can see.

check-1.text: This withdrawal matches exactly one earlier deposit, 7 blocks before. Anonymity set: one.

plan-0.text: Pre-flight checks a transfer before you make it. Say, 7.7 ZEC from Ironwood to an exchange.

plan-1.text: Only one other recent transfer used that amount. Privacy score: 25 out of 100.

plan-2.text: The fix: standard ZIP-318 denominations at random intervals, each hiding among hundreds of look-alikes.

scan-0.text: Scan finds the leaks in your own wallet. It decrypts on your device; the viewing key never leaves the browser.

scan-1.text: Here, coins were deshielded and immediately re-shielded: a critical round trip, linked with certainty.

sdk-0.text: Wallet developers get the same engine as an SDK: one call to checkSend, before the user hits send.

outro-0.text: Leakscope. See the leak before you send. Open source, at leakscope-cyan.vercel.app.
